Kenna: Heads up — since the tokenizer tweak landed on deckhand-v1 we've seen p99 latency jump for long-context (>= 16k) requests. Started ~08:20 UTC.
Miguel: seeing the same in our dashboards, p95 fine but p99 up ~2.4x on hosted. Any errors in logs? :eyes:
Kenna: no 500s. Mostly big tail on decode time and KV cache misses. Example request id: rdw-req-8f3a.
Cheng: can you paste a stacktrace or runtime span for that request id?
Kenna: pasted trace (trimmed):
```
service: inference
model: deckhand-v1
seq_len: 18432
phase: decode
span: kv_cache_lookup -> 120ms (expected 4ms)
span: attention_forward -> 90ms
span: tokenizer.split -> 42ms (new bpe mapping)
total_tokens: 15360
```
Miguel: kv_cache_lookup 120ms is huge — suggests cache invalidation or key mismatched. Tokenizer.split 42ms also suspicious. That mapping change altered token boundary counts?
Alyssa: quick repro steps I ran:
1) POST /v1/generate with header `x-rdw-model: deckhand-v1`
2) payload with prompt length ~16k chars and `max_tokens: 2k`
3) set `trace: true`
Result: p99 decode reproduction locally using hosted canary.
Miguel: repro confirmed. Repro script (sanitized):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.rdw.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-rdw-model: deckhand-v1" \
  -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>...","max_tokens":2000,"stream":false}'
```
Kenna: hypothesis: tokenizer mapping increased token count for certain CJK/emoji sequences causing more KV keys -> more cache churn and mismatched key normalization between loader and runtime. Also possible new tokenizer uses different byte offsets so KV cache lookup misses.
Cheng: checked commit: `tokenizer: bpe-v3 mapping for deckhand` — there was a normalization change. Also a runtime change to expire KV entries earlier in the same PR. Combined could explain 2x p99.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-7423 assigned to eng-ml and eng-runtime.
Alyssa: immediate mitigation options:
- pin requests routing to deckhand-v1-legacy-tokenizer (we still serve legacy variant)
- increase kv_cache TTL to avoid premature eviction (quick toggle in feature flags)
- temporary rate-limit very large contexts for hosted tier
- revert tokenizer mapping on canary
Which one should we try first?
Miguel: toggle KV TTL as a fast toggle, and route affected customers to legacy tokenizer for now. I can push KV TTL flag in 5m.
Kenna: routing to legacy tokenizer helped in canary — p99 dropped to baseline within 12m. Logs show cache hit rate increased from 62% -> 94%.
Cheng: opened PR to revert the normalization line and add unit test for byte-offset consistency. PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4521
Alyssa: notes for support replies: mention we identified tokenizer + KV eviction interaction, mitigating by routing to legacy tokenizer and increasing KV TTL. Offering to onboard affected customers to dedicated pools if they need sustained long-context performance.
Kenna: follow-ups: 1) validate no correctness regressions after tokenizer revert (eval set), 2) add smoke test: long-context kv cache hit rate >= 90% for 16k+ prompts before promotion, 3) add metric alarm for sudden kv hit rate drops.
Miguel: I'm on the flag rollout and routing change. Will post updates.
ops-bot: update INC-2026-7423 status -> mitigated (routing + TTL), assigned -> eng-ml for root cause.
Miguel: rollout done. Monitoring shows p99 back to expected for canary and gradual improvement in hosted.
Kenna: closing loop with customer support: sending apology + mitigation steps + ETA for permanent fix.
Alyssa: creating a postmortem stub and tagging eng-ml, eng-runtime, support. We'll flesh out RCA after tokenizer revert lands and canaries pass. :white_check_mark:
Cheng: one more action — add synthetic to run weekly that constructs edge-case tokens (CJK+emoji overlap) to validate token counts vs baseline.
Kenna: thanks team. If anyone hits residual regressions ping me directly.
